newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares lower in quiet trade ahead of budget.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares lower in quiet trade ahead of budget.

text.p: Delhi shares traded lower in subdued afternoon trade on Friday on profit-taking and selective selling by speculators ahead of a vote on the 1997/98 (April-March) budget in parliament, brokers said.
At 12:45 p.m. (0715 GMT), the Delhi Stock Exchange's benchmark index dipped 9.93 points to 792.31.
"It seems speculators are waiting for the budget to get parliament's approval before finalising their strategy," said Harish Malhotra of brokers Malhotra Financial Consultants.
Parliament is due to consider the federal budget, presented in February by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram next week and vote on May 9.
Brokers earlier said trading was slack due to a corruption scandal involving a ruling party leader.
They said worries over the federal police's decision to prosecute Laloo Prasad Yadav, who is the president of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's Janata Dal party, hit the market.
Yadav says he is innocent but has refused to accept opposition demands that he must step down and face trial.
State Bank of India quoted 5.45 rupees down at 314.45.
